domain: Moral Philosophy / Historical Ethics / Commitment Systems
topic_summary: Analysis of Spartan infant exposure as a historical instantiation of a personhood-boundary kernel, examining whether the ancient practice represents a reading now structurally unreachable from modern moral frameworks or a reading that has been suppressed/abandoned. Tests whether moral possibility-space contraction is path-dependent naturalization or genuine constraint discovery.

key_entities: Spartan state (authority claiming right to determine infant viability)
Gerousia (council of elders administering exposure decisions)
Modern human rights framework (contemporary authority claiming universal infant personhood)
Hillside exposure site (Apothetae, physical mechanism of exclusion)
key_tensions: State eugenic authority vs parental autonomy (Spartan practice vs modern family rights)
Conditional personhood vs inherent personhood (exposure-permitting vs exposure-prohibiting readings)
Historical moral diversity vs moral progress narrative (relativist vs universalist interpretations)

commitment_system_recognition.kernel_description: The personhood-boundary kernel: the threshold at which a human organism acquires moral standing sufficient to prohibit deliberate killing
commitment_system_recognition.authority_description: Competing interpretive authorities: ancient civic-eugenic frameworks grounded in polis survival vs modern rights frameworks grounded in inherent human dignity
commitment_system_recognition.candidate_pattern: Interpretive Capture (modern framework denies legitimacy of alternative readings)

readings.commitment: Personhood contingent on civic viability assessment; state authority to exclude defective infants from moral community
readings.authority_grounding: Polis survival necessity; collective welfare trumps individual infant claims
readings.expected_structural_delta: Infants enter victim set only after passing state viability test; high beneficiary concentration in warrior class; exposure mechanism institutionalized as legitimate state function

readings.commitment: Personhood begins at live birth; parental authority over infant fate but not state eugenic authority
readings.authority_grounding: Roman patria potestas tradition; family sovereignty over household members
readings.expected_structural_delta: Infants enter victim set at birth but parents retain exposure authority; moderate beneficiary concentration in paterfamilias; exposure privatized rather than state-administered

readings.commitment: Personhood inherent at biological humanity threshold (conception/viability/birth); no legitimate authority to exclude
readings.authority_grounding: Universal human rights framework; Kantian dignity; religious imago dei traditions
readings.expected_structural_delta: All live-born infants in victim set; zero legitimate exposure authority; exposure reclassified as murder; beneficiary diffusion across rights-holders

axiom_contradictions.basis: Civic-eugenic reading holds personhood is contingent on state assessment of civic viability; inherent-dignity reading holds personhood is non-contingent property of human organisms. No framework can simultaneously hold both that personhood is contingent on external assessment AND that it is inherent/non-contingent.

Birth-threshold reading grants parental authority to exclude post-birth infants from personhood; inherent-dignity reading denies any legitimate authority to exclude. No framework can simultaneously hold both that parents have legitimate exclusion authority AND that no such authority exists.

omegas.description: Extent of actual Spartan exposure practice contested among historians. Plutarch's account may be idealized/exaggerated. If practice was rare/mythologized, civic-eugenic reading may be theoretical rather than institutionally realized.
omegas.source: Extraction phase: absence of primary Spartan sources; reliance on later Greek/Roman accounts

omegas.description: Whether resource scarcity made exposure necessary (mountain) or merely removed constraint against it (removed rope). If mountain, civic-eugenic reading may be contingent on material conditions rather than pure moral framework choice.

Birth-threshold and civic-eugenic readings may collapse if parental discretion and state authority are merely different enforcement mechanisms for same underlying personhood threshold. Independence depends on whether authority-location is structural or incidental.
omegas.source: §3 Independence Testing: potential Type A overlap between readings

omegas.description: Core question: Is inherent-dignity reading a discovered constraint (civic-eugenic reading was always wrong) or path-dependent naturalization (we cannot now reach civic-eugenic reading but it was once genuinely available)? Answer determines whether moral progress is discovery or drift.
omegas.source: Deferred axis: possibility_space_contraction; founding motivation of analysis

omegas.description: Selective abortion, neonatal euthanasia for severe defects, and allocation of neonatal intensive care may instantiate civic-eugenic logic under different framings. If so, reading may not be unreachable but merely re-routed through medical rather than civic authority.
omegas.source: Dark Matter Probe 2 (Absence Inventory): modern practices not addressed in extraction
